Trying to get a job, a lot of the ones I'm interested in require a "clean driving record". 2, almost 3 years ago I got a careless driving conviction. I've since moved across the country.

I assume when they do a driving record check, they'll see it and most likely immediately deny me. But, just in case, I'm asking here to see what you all have to say.
How likely is it that a "careless driving" conviction will show up on a background search after moving to a different state
Pretty good if their PI that does the investigations is any good.
I used to do background checks. Was it an infraction or misdemeanor?
Infraction/traffic/ordinance violation. All basically synonymous with "less than a misdemeanor" in most states. Though some do have a title called "minor misdemeanor".

It will show, all states are connected. It's a basic search now a days. However, when they say clean driving record, it's generally for DUI and accidents. Also they usually stop caring if it was 3 years or older. Depends on the company. Years ago I had a small issue with my driving record, and the company hired me and worked around it. It's all about them getting you insured, that's all they care about.

Clean, as in not suspended, dui, or vehicular homicide convictions. 3 year old carless probably wouldn't even show on basic background search. Most places don't spend for anything thurough. The only time basic moving violations, like careless driving, matter is if you you get too many and your license gets suspended.

Depending on the severity, the record could be reported up to 7 years. Weather or not the company judges those crimes important or not depends on the company. 3 years is a very "recent" time in a background investigation. Not to scare OP or anything.

OP said it was careless driving. That is a minor moving violation that is typically given if the cop is nice and doesn't want to write a speeding ticket or you plea down fighting in court. This violation is removed from record after 36 months. Its with felonies they search 7 years back.
Felonies and misdemeanors. And you can report records even farther back if they were convictions.

In my area, "careless driving" is something you plead to in court (more fees, zero points). If they find it, just say "I was late to an [insert thing here], got caught speeding, Instead of taking the 1 point on my license I figured I'd keep the 0 points and get a lawyer."
